mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% consistently compresses equity discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors shift from fixed income to equities.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 0.5 percentage point decline in unemployment rate over three months signals labor market tightening, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days through improved consumer spending momentum.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered periods, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 for the trigger condition.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates robust demand, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days via strengthened corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS exceed their 3-month moving averages, or the interaction term Rank IC is negative.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production below 100 combined with restrictive monetary policy (FEDFUNDS > 2.0%) signals recessionary supply pressures, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: recessionary supply shock with restrictive policy
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered periods, or the regime-specific Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI inflation exceeding 2.5% triggers Fed tightening expectations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days through reduced equity valuation multiples.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods with CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) above 2.0% consistently correlates with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as stronger economic activity supports corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods with GDPC1 growth > 2.0%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent employment growth (PAYEMS) and unemployment decline (UNRATE) signal labor market tightness, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days through elevated consumer spending and profit margins.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls, or the interaction effect Rank IC is negative.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO) over three months typically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as manufacturing weakness signals broader economic deceleration.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO declines, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.
